content.text:
Yes: the project already retains the Parliament identifiers needed for declaration links.

- Parliament’s interest ID becomes `declarations.source_declaration_id`, then API `declaration.source_id`: [schema](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/db/migrations/20260915000000_initial.up.sql:21), [API response](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/inbound/http/handlers/entity_details.rs:94).
- Both views already display that identifier as “Declaration …”. Those are the natural places for “View Parliament source” links: [member view](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/src/MemberDeclarations.svelte:18), [funder view](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/src/FunderDeclarations.svelte:25).
- The member API’s `id` is the Parliament member ID, so a member-register fallback also needs no backend changes: [repository](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/entity_details.rs:27).

Recommend linking each declaration group to the verified Parliament interest page, with all funding rows in that group sharing the source. Our individual funding IDs are generated from member/declaration/register/ordinal, rather than separate Parliament entry IDs: [identifier construction](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_cleaning.rs:250). The loader persists these IDs, but the detail API does not expose them.

Historical limit: acquisition includes expired declarations and all available registers, but selects the newest version of each interest. Register IDs and publication dates survive in pipeline artifacts ([capture schema](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_ingestion.rs:107)), but are absent from the declaration database/API. Exact links to the register edition used would therefore require exposing/persisting that provenance. Existing IDs suffice for declaration-level links, subject to Parliament’s historical URL support.
